inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL report uses FIRST_VALUE over a partition ordered by a descending measure to repeat the partition's highest value on each row.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored cluster-reading report. The query partitions decimal readings by cluster, orders NULL readings after measured values, and combines FIRST_VALUE, NTH_VALUE, and LAST_VALUE over an explicit full ROWS frame. The schema, rows, names, and monitoring purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Cluster 10 has two measured readings and one NULL reading; descending order places NULL last, so FIRST_VALUE is the peak, NTH_VALUE(..., 2) is the lower measured reading, and LAST_VALUE is NULL across the explicit full frame. Cluster 20 has two measured readings and confirms the same value-window semantics without a NULL tail.
determinism_notes: Each window orders by reading DESC plus unique reading_id, and the final result orders by cluster_id plus reading_id. All timestamps, values, and IDs are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE cluster_readings (reading_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cluster_id INT NOT NULL, reading DECIMAL(8,2) NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT cluster_id, reading_id, reading, FIRST_VALUE(reading) OVER (PARTITION BY cluster_id ORDER BY reading DESC, reading_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS peak_reading, NTH_VALUE(reading, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY cluster_id ORDER BY reading DESC, reading_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS second_reading, LAST_VALUE(reading) OVER (PARTITION BY cluster_id ORDER BY reading DESC, reading_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS tail_reading FROM cluster_readings ORDER BY cluster_id, reading_id
